subproblem.title: Uniqueness of the approximate tangent plane of a rectifiable varifold
subproblem.statement: For all n, ℓ, every rectifiable n-varifold V in ℝ^{n+ℓ}, every x ∈ ℝ^{n+ℓ} and all linear subspaces P, Q: if V.IsApproxTangentAt x P and V.IsApproxTangentAt x Q (each: the subspace is n-dimensional and, for some constant c > 0, t⁻ⁿ∫ f(t⁻¹(y − x)) dμ_V(y) → c∫ f dHⁿ over the subspace as t ↓ 0 for every f ∈ C_c), then P = Q.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n ℓ : ℕ) (V : RectifiableVarifold n ℓ) (x : Ambient n ℓ) (P Q : Submodule ℝ (Ambient n ℓ)), V.IsApproxTangentAt x P → V.IsApproxTangentAt x Q → P = Q
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: the parent proof, step 5(ii) (Simon Ch. 3, Remark 1.5(1) and the uniqueness remark after Ch. 3, 1.7 / Ch. 4, 1.3: the blow-up limit determines the plane). No errata apply.

Conventions. E := Ambient n ℓ; Hⁿ := μHE[n]; μ_V := V.weight; C_c(E) := C_c(E, ℝ). V.IsApproxTangentAt x P means: finrank P = n and there is c > 0 such that for every f ∈ C_c(E), (tⁿ)⁻¹∫ f(t⁻¹(y − x)) dμ_V(y) → c·∫_P f dHⁿ as t ↓ 0 (filter 𝓝[>] 0).
Results used (pinned; standard axioms only): SimonGMT Chapter03.regular_euclideanHausdorffMeasure_restrict_submodule (finrank P = n ⇒ Hⁿ⌞P is a regular measure); SimonGMT Chapter03.support_euclideanHausdorffMeasure_restrict_submodule (finrank P = n ⇒ support(Hⁿ⌞P) = P as a set); Mathlib Measure.Regular.smul (a·ν is regular whenever ν is regular and a ∈ [0, ∞) is a finite scalar); Mathlib Measure.ext_of_integral_eq_on_compactlySupported (two regular measures on a locally compact Hausdorff Borel space with equal integrals of all f ∈ C_c are equal); Mathlib integral_smul_measure.

Proof.
1. By hypothesis finrank P = finrank Q = n and there are c > 0 and c' > 0 such that, for every f ∈ C_c(E), the same function t ↦ (tⁿ)⁻¹∫ f(t⁻¹(y − x)) dμ_V(y) tends to c·∫_P f dHⁿ and to c'·∫_Q f dHⁿ along 𝓝[>] 0. This filter on ℝ is not trivial (NeBot), and limits in ℝ are unique (tendsto_nhds_unique), so
c·∫_P f dHⁿ = c'·∫_Q f dHⁿ for every f ∈ C_c(E).   (1.1)
2. Let λ_P := ofReal(c)·(Hⁿ⌞P) and λ_Q := ofReal(c')·(Hⁿ⌞Q). For f ∈ C_c(E), ∫ f dλ_P = (ofReal c).toReal·∫_P f dHⁿ = c·∫_P f dHⁿ (integral_smul_measure, c ≥ 0), and likewise ∫ f dλ_Q = c'·∫_Q f dHⁿ; by (1.1), ∫ f dλ_P = ∫ f dλ_Q for every f ∈ C_c(E).
3. Hⁿ⌞P and Hⁿ⌞Q are regular (Chapter03.regular_euclideanHausdorffMeasure_restrict_submodule, since finrank P = finrank Q = n), so λ_P and λ_Q are regular (Measure.Regular.smul, ofReal c ≠ ∞, ofReal c' ≠ ∞). E is a finite-dimensional normed space, hence locally compact and Hausdorff with its Borel σ-algebra. By Measure.ext_of_integral_eq_on_compactlySupported, λ_P = λ_Q.
4. For a measure ν and a ∈ (0, ∞), support(a·ν) = support(ν): a point z is in the support of a measure iff every neighbourhood U of z has positive measure, and (a·ν)(U) = a·ν(U) > 0 iff ν(U) > 0 (a ≠ 0, a ≠ ∞). Since ofReal c > 0 and ofReal c' > 0 (c, c' > 0),
support(Hⁿ⌞P) = support(λ_P) = support(λ_Q) = support(Hⁿ⌞Q).
By Chapter03.support_euclideanHausdorffMeasure_restrict_submodule the left side is the set P and the right side is the set Q. Thus (P : Set E) = (Q : Set E), and P = Q as submodules (SetLike.ext'). ∎

proof_key_steps: Uniqueness of limits along 𝓝[>] 0 gives c∫_P f dHⁿ = c'∫_Q f dHⁿ for every f ∈ C_c
c·Hⁿ⌞P and c'·Hⁿ⌞Q are regular with the same C_c integrals, hence equal (Measure.ext_of_integral_eq_on_compactlySupported)
Positive multiples have the same support, and supp(Hⁿ⌞P) = P, supp(Hⁿ⌞Q) = Q, so P = Q

subproblem.title: Closed-ball density from the weighted blow-up (Simon Ch. 3, 1.8(2))
subproblem.statement: Let n ≥ 1, ℓ ≥ 0, μ a Borel measure on E = ℝ^{n+ℓ} that is finite on compact sets, x ∈ E, P an n-dimensional linear subspace and c > 0 such that t⁻ⁿ∫ f(t⁻¹(y − x)) dμ(y) → c∫_P f dHⁿ as t ↓ 0 for every f ∈ C_c(E, ℝ). Then μ(B_ρ(x))/(ω_n ρⁿ) → c as ρ ↓ 0, where B_ρ(x) is the closed ball, μ(B_ρ(x)) is taken as a real number (μ.real) and ω_n = omega n.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n ℓ : ℕ) (μ : Measure (Ambient n ℓ)) (x : Ambient n ℓ) (P : Submodule ℝ (Ambient n ℓ)) (c : ℝ), 0 < n → IsFiniteMeasureOnCompacts μ → Module.finrank ℝ P = n → 0 < c → (∀ f : C_c(Ambient n ℓ, ℝ), Tendsto (fun t : ℝ ↦ (t ^ n)⁻¹ * ∫ y, f (t⁻¹ • (y - x)) ∂μ) (𝓝[>] 0) (𝓝 (c * ∫ y in (P : Set (Ambient n ℓ)), f y ∂μHE[n]))) → Tendsto (fun ρ : ℝ ↦ μ.real (closedBall x ρ) / (omega n * ρ ^ n)) (𝓝[>] 0) (𝓝 c)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: the parent proof, step 5(iv) (Simon Ch. 3, Remark 1.8(2), written with closed balls and Simon's ωₙ = omega n). No errata apply.

Conventions. n ≥ 1, ℓ ≥ 0; E := Ambient n ℓ; ℝⁿ := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) with Lebesgue measure Lⁿ := volume; Hⁿ := μHE[n]; B_ρ(z) := closedBall z ρ; ω_n := omega n = Lⁿ(ball 0 1).toReal; μ.real(S) := (μ S).toReal; η_t(y) := t⁻¹(y − x). Hypotheses: μ is a (Borel) measure on E with μ(K) < ∞ for every compact K; finrank P = n; c > 0; and (H) for every f ∈ C_c(E, ℝ), (tⁿ)⁻¹∫ f(η_t(y)) dμ(y) → c·∫_P f dHⁿ as t ↓ 0.
Results used (pinned; standard axioms only): Mathlib InnerProductSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume, InnerProductSpace.volume_closedBall, InnerProductSpace.volume_ball, Isometry.map_euclideanHausdorffMeasure (as used in SimonGMT Chapter04.planeMeasure_unit_closedBall), Measure.addHaar_closedBall_eq_addHaar_ball.

Proof.
1. Balls in the plane: Hⁿ(P ∩ B_s(0)) = ω_n·sⁿ for every s ≥ 0, and in particular 0 < ω_n < ∞. Indeed, the inclusion ι: P → E is a linear isometry with range P, so Hⁿ⌞P = ι_*(Hⁿ_P) where Hⁿ_P is the n-dimensional Euclidean Hausdorff measure of the n-dimensional inner product space P (Isometry.map_euclideanHausdorffMeasure); Hⁿ_P = volume_P (InnerProductSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume, finrank P = n); ι⁻¹(B_s(0)) is the closed ball of radius s in P; and by InnerProductSpace.volume_closedBall (P is nontrivial since n ≥ 1), volume_P(closedBall 0 s) = ofReal(s)ⁿ·ofReal(√πⁿ/Γ(n/2 + 1)), while by InnerProductSpace.volume_ball for ℝⁿ (finrank n), Lⁿ(ball 0 1) = ofReal(√πⁿ/Γ(n/2 + 1)) — the same constant, whose real value is ω_n ∈ (0, ∞). Hence Hⁿ(P ∩ B_s(0)) = ofReal(ω_n sⁿ). In particular Hⁿ⌞P is finite on bounded sets, so every f ∈ C_c(E, ℝ) is Hⁿ⌞P-integrable.
2. Cut-off functions. For δ ∈ (0, 1) define f_δ⁺(y) := min(1, max(0, (1 + δ − |y|)/δ)) and f_δ⁻(y) := min(1, max(0, (1 − |y|)/δ)). Both are continuous with values in [0, 1] and vanish outside the compact set B_{1+δ}(0), so they belong to C_c(E, ℝ). Moreover f_δ⁺ = 1 on B_1(0) and f_δ⁺ = 0 outside B_{1+δ}(0); f_δ⁻ = 1 on B_{1−δ}(0) and f_δ⁻(y) = 0 whenever |y| ≥ 1. (One may instead use SimonGMT Chapter04.tangentDensityCutoff and a rescaled copy.)
3. Sandwich. Let t > 0. Since |η_t(y)| ≤ 1 ⟺ y ∈ B_t(x), we have for all y: f_δ⁻(η_t(y)) ≤ 1_{B_t(x)}(y) ≤ f_δ⁺(η_t(y)) (if f_δ⁻(η_t(y)) > 0 then |η_t(y)| < 1). All three functions are nonnegative, bounded by 1, Borel, and vanish outside the compact set B_{2t}(x), which has finite μ-measure; integrating,
∫ f_δ⁻∘η_t dμ ≤ μ(B_t(x)) ≤ ∫ f_δ⁺∘η_t dμ,   (3.1)
and μ(B_t(x)) < ∞, so μ.real(B_t(x)) = μ(B_t(x)).toReal satisfies the same inequalities.
4. Limits of the bounds. By (H), (tⁿ)⁻¹∫ f_δ^±∘η_t dμ → c·∫_P f_δ^± dHⁿ. Since 1_{B_{1−δ}(0)} ≤ f_δ⁻ and f_δ⁺ ≤ 1_{B_{1+δ}(0)}, step 1 gives ∫_P f_δ⁻ dHⁿ ≥ Hⁿ(P ∩ B_{1−δ}(0)) = ω_n(1 − δ)ⁿ and ∫_P f_δ⁺ dHⁿ ≤ Hⁿ(P ∩ B_{1+δ}(0)) = ω_n(1 + δ)ⁿ. As c > 0: c·∫_P f_δ⁻ ≥ cω_n(1 − δ)ⁿ and c·∫_P f_δ⁺ ≤ cω_n(1 + δ)ⁿ.
5. Conclusion. Let q(t) := μ.real(B_t(x))/(ω_n·tⁿ) for t > 0. Given ε' > 0 choose δ ∈ (0, 1) with c((1 + δ)ⁿ − 1) < ε'/2 and c(1 − (1 − δ)ⁿ) < ε'/2. By step 4 there is t_0 > 0 such that for 0 < t < t_0: (tⁿ)⁻¹∫ f_δ⁺∘η_t dμ < cω_n(1 + δ)ⁿ + ω_nε'/2 and (tⁿ)⁻¹∫ f_δ⁻∘η_t dμ > cω_n(1 − δ)ⁿ − ω_nε'/2. By (3.1), dividing by ω_n > 0, for 0 < t < t_0: c − ε' < c(1 − δ)ⁿ − ε'/2 < q(t) < c(1 + δ)ⁿ + ε'/2 < c + ε'. Hence q(t) → c as t ↓ 0, i.e. Tendsto (fun ρ ↦ μ.real (closedBall x ρ) / (omega n * ρ ^ n)) (𝓝[>] 0) (𝓝 c). ∎

Implementation note (not part of the argument): the statement elaborates with the frozen imports; the proof may need additional imports such as Mathlib.MeasureTheory.Measure.Lebesgue.VolumeOfBalls and Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter04.TangentDensity (built in the pinned packages); the frozen child types elaborate unchanged with such imports.
proof_key_steps: Hⁿ(P ∩ B_s(0)) = ω_n sⁿ via the isometry of P with an n-dimensional Euclidean space
Cut-offs f_δ^± ∈ C_c with f_δ^−(t⁻¹(y − x)) ≤ 1_{B_t(x)}(y) ≤ f_δ^+(t⁻¹(y − x))
The limits c∫_P f_δ^± lie between cω_n(1 − δ)ⁿ and cω_n(1 + δ)ⁿ
Let δ ↓ 0: μ(B_t(x))/(ω_n tⁿ) → c

audit.reason: The finite-on-compacts hypothesis justifies the real integrals and μ.real. The explicit cutoff sandwich and plane-ball normalization prove precisely the closed-ball density limit with omega n.

subproblem.statement: For all n, ℓ, every admissible pair a = (M, θ) in E = ℝ^{n+ℓ}, every x ∈ E and every n-dimensional subspace P: if t⁻ⁿ∫ f(t⁻¹(y − x)) dμ_{v(M,θ)}(y) → θ(x)∫_P f dHⁿ as t ↓ 0 for every f ∈ C_c(E, ℝ), then HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M θ x P (Simon Ch. 3, 1.7), i.e. ∫_{η_{x,r}(M)} f(y)θ(x + ry) dHⁿ(y) → θ(x)∫_P f dHⁿ as r ↓ 0 for every f ∈ C_c(E, ℝ), where η_{x,r}(y) = r⁻¹(y − x).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n ℓ : ℕ) (a : RectifiablePair n ℓ) (x : Ambient n ℓ) (P : Submodule ℝ (Ambient n ℓ)), Module.finrank ℝ P = n → (∀ f : C_c(Ambient n ℓ, ℝ), Tendsto (fun t : ℝ ↦ (t ^ n)⁻¹ * ∫ y, f (t⁻¹ • (y - x)) ∂(mk a).weight) (𝓝[>] 0) (𝓝 (a.θ x * ∫ y in (P : Set (Ambient n ℓ)), f y ∂μHE[n]))) → Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter03.HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n a.M a.θ x P

Conventions. E := Ambient n ℓ; Hⁿ := μHE[n]; a = (M, θ) is an admissible pair (M Hⁿ-null-measurable, θ > 0 on M, θ integrable on M ∩ K for compact K); μ := (mk a).weight = pairWeight n M θ = (Hⁿ⌞M).withDensity(ofReal ∘ θ) (definitional for the class of a); η_r := Chapter03.blowUpMap x r, η_r(y) = r⁻¹(y − x). subproblem.statement: Let n ≥ 1, ℓ ≥ 0, a = (M, θ) an admissible pair in E = ℝ^{n+ℓ}, V = v(M, θ) with weight μ_V and tangent spaces T_x = V.tangentSpace x. Assume: N₀ ⊆ E is Borel with Hⁿ(N₀) = 0; (C_i, F_i)_{i∈ℕ} are Lipschitz pieces (C_i ⊆ ℝⁿ compact, F_i Lipschitz, differentiable on C_i with injective DF_i, DF_i continuous on C_i, c_i|v − w| ≤ |F_i(v) − F_i(w)| on C_i with c_i > 0) with M ⊆ N₀ ∪ ⋃_i F_i(C_i); for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M, T_x = DF_i(w)(ℝⁿ) for every i and every w ∈ C_i with F_i(w) = x; and x ↦ p_{T_x} is a.e. strongly measurable for Hⁿ⌞M. subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: the parent proof, steps 7–10 (Simon Ch. 4, 2.1–2.2 with the area formula of Ch. 3 §2, 2.4–2.5, and the computation of Ch. 2 §5, 5.2–5.3). The parent's references to its steps 4–6 ("T_i(x) = T_x for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M_i", "x ↦ p_x is μ-a.e. strongly measurable", "dim T_x = n a.e.") are replaced by the hypotheses of this theorem (step 0 below). No errata apply.

Conventions. n ≥ 1, ℓ ≥ 0; E := Ambient n ℓ; ℝⁿ := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) with Lebesgue measure Lⁿ; Hⁿ := μHE[n]; B_ρ(z) := closedBall z ρ. a = (M, θ) is an admissible pair (IsRectifiablePair: M countably n-rectifiable and Hⁿ-null-measurable, θ > 0 on M, θ integrable on M ∩ K for every compact K), V := mk a, μ := V.weight, T_x := V.tangentSpace x, p_x := T_x.starProjection, div_M X(x) := V.tangentialDiv X x = trace(DX(x) ∘ p_x). For a subspace P ⊆ E with inclusion ι_P and Λ ∈ L(E, E) put J^P(Λ) := normDet(Λ ∘ ι_P) ≥ 0 (Mathlib LinearMap.normDet of Λ.domRestrict P); for an orthonormal basis e_1, …, e_k of P, J^P(Λ)² = det[⟨Λe_a, Λe_b⟩]_{a,b≤k} (Mathlib LinearMap.normDet_sq_eq_det_gram), J^{0}(Λ) = 1, and J^P(Λ)² = det S_P(Λ) with S_P(Λ) := p_P Λ*Λ p_P + I − p_P ∈ L(E, E) (Λ* = ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint Λ). Proof of the last identity: take an orthonormal basis e_1, …, e_{n+ℓ} of E with e_1, …, e_k a basis of P and e_{k+1}, …, e_{n+ℓ} a basis of P^⊥ (k = dim P). Since p_P is self-adjoint, p_Pe_a = e_a for a ≤ k and p_Pe_b = 0 for b > k, the matrix ⟨S_P(Λ)e_a, e_b⟩ has entries ⟨Λe_a, Λe_b⟩ for a, b ≤ k, entries δ_{ab} for a, b > k, and 0 in the mixed blocks (for a ≤ k < b: ⟨p_PΛ*Λe_a, e_b⟩ = ⟨Λ*Λe_a, p_Pe_b⟩ = 0 and ⟨S_P(Λ)e_b, e_a⟩ = ⟨Λ*Λp_Pe_b, p_Pe_a⟩ + ⟨e_b − p_Pe_b, e_a⟩ = 0 + ⟨e_b, e_a⟩ = 0); hence det S_P(Λ) = det[⟨Λe_a, Λe_b⟩]_{a,b≤k} = J^P(Λ)² by LinearMap.normDet_sq_eq_det_gram (for k = 0 both sides are 1). Consequently J^P(Λ) = (det S_P(Λ))^{1/2} is a continuous function of the pair (Λ, p_P) (polynomial in the entries, followed by the square root of a nonnegative number). For G: ℝⁿ → E, JG(v) := (fderiv ℝ G v).normDet (SimonGMT Chapter02.areaJacobianAt).
Hypotheses: (h1) N₀ ⊆ E Borel with Hⁿ(N₀) = 0; (h2) for each i ∈ ℕ, (C_i, F_i) is a Lipschitz piece: C_i ⊆ ℝⁿ compact, F_i: ℝⁿ → E Lipschitz, F_i differentiable at each w ∈ C_i with injective DF_i(w), DF_i continuous on C_i, c_i|v − w| ≤ |F_i(v) − F_i(w)| on C_i with c_i > 0; (h3) M ⊆ N₀ ∪ ⋃_i F_i(C_i); (h4) for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M: for all i and all w ∈ C_i with F_i(w) = x, T_x = range DF_i(w); (h5) x ↦ p_x is a.e.-strongly measurable for Hⁿ⌞M; (h6) IsCompactVariation φ ε K: ε > 0, K compact, Φ(t, y) := φ t y is C^∞ on U := (−ε, ε) × E, for t ∈ (−ε, ε) φ_t := φ t is bijective with C^∞ inverse Function.invFun φ_t, φ_0 = id, and φ_t(y) = y for t ∈ (−ε, ε), y ∉ K. X(y) := deriv (t ↦ φ t y) 0.
Results used (pinned; standard axioms only): (R2a) SimonGMT Chapter02.weighted_area_formula_lipschitz_injOn (∫⁻_{G(B)} u dHⁿ = ∫⁻_B ofReal(JG(v))·u(G(v)) dLⁿ(v) for Lipschitz G, Borel B, G injective on B, any u: E → [0, ∞]); (R2b) SimonGMT Chapter02.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image_le_of_lipschitzOn; Mathlib LinearMap.normDet_comp (normDet(Λ ∘ A') = normDet(Λ restricted to range A')·normDet(A'); also SimonGMT Chapter02.areaJacobian_comp_eq_parametrization_mul_tangential), LinearMap.normDet_sq_eq_det_gram, ContDiffAt.isSymmSndFDerivAt (symmetry of second derivatives), hasDerivAt_integral_of_dominated_loc_of_deriv_le (differentiation under the integral sign), lintegral_iUnion₀, integral_withDensity_eq_integral_toReal_smul₀, ofReal_integral_eq_lintegral_ofReal, withDensity_absolutelyContinuous, AEStronglyMeasurable.mono_ac, LinearMap.finrank_range_of_inj.

Proof.

0. Consequences of the hypotheses.
(0a) For Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M, dim T_x = n: Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M lies outside N₀ (h1), hence (h3) x = F_i(w) for some i and w ∈ C_i; by (h4) T_x = range DF_i(w), whose dimension is dim ℝⁿ = n because DF_i(w) is injective (LinearMap.finrank_range_of_inj, finrank_euclideanSpace_fin).
(0b) μ = (Hⁿ⌞M).withDensity(ofReal ∘ θ) (definition of the weight on the class mk a). θ is a.e.-strongly measurable for Hⁿ⌞M (it is integrable on each M ∩ B_k(0)); μ(S) = ∫⁻_{M∩S} ofReal θ dHⁿ for Borel S, so μ is finite on compact sets; μ ≪ Hⁿ⌞M (withDensity_absolutelyContinuous); and for every Borel S and every g: E → ℝ, ∫_S g dμ = ∫_{M∩S} gθ dHⁿ (integral_withDensity_eq_integral_toReal_smul₀ — no integrability assumption is needed — together with (ofReal θ(z)).toReal = θ(z) for z ∈ M, which holds Hⁿ⌞M-a.e. by ae_restrict_mem₀).
(0c) By (h5) and μ ≪ Hⁿ⌞M, x ↦ p_x is also μ-a.e. strongly measurable (AEStronglyMeasurable.mono_ac).

1. The variation (parent step 7).
(a) Φ is C^∞ on the open set U. X(y) = DΦ(0, y)(1, 0) (chain rule for t ↦ (t, y)), so X is C^∞ on E. For y ∉ K, Φ(t, y) = y for all t ∈ (−ε, ε), hence X(y) = 0; since E ∖ K is open (K is compact, hence closed), DX = 0 on E ∖ K, and therefore div_M X(x) = trace(0 ∘ p_x) = 0 for every x ∉ K.
(b) Let t ∈ (−ε, ε). φ_t = Φ(t, ·) is C^∞, bijective, with C^∞ inverse ψ_t := Function.invFun φ_t, which is a two-sided inverse (Function.leftInverse_invFun / rightInverse_invFun for the bijection φ_t). Differentiating ψ_t ∘ φ_t = id gives Dψ_t(φ_t(y)) ∘ Dφ_t(y) = I, so Dφ_t(y) is invertible for every y; φ_t is a homeomorphism. On the open set E ∖ K, φ_t = id, so Dφ_t(y) = I there; y ↦ Dφ_t(y) is continuous, hence bounded on K, so sup_y ‖Dφ_t(y)‖ < ∞ and φ_t is Lipschitz (mean value inequality on the convex set E). By (R2b), Hⁿ(φ_t(Z)) = 0 whenever Hⁿ(Z) = 0; images of Borel sets under the homeomorphism φ_t are Borel. Consequently φ_t maps Hⁿ-null-measurable sets to Hⁿ-null-measurable sets (a null-measurable set is a Borel set plus a subset of a null set).
(c) The partial derivative (t, y) ↦ Dφ_t(y) is C^∞ on U, and by the symmetry of the second derivative of Φ at (0, y) (ContDiffAt.isSymmSndFDerivAt), ∂_t Dφ_t(y)|_{t=0} = D_y(∂_tΦ(0, ·))(y) = DX(y). Also Dφ_0(y) = I since φ_0 = id.

2. Area formula on M (parent step 8; Simon Ch. 3, 2.4–2.5). For t ∈ (−ε, ε) and x ∈ E let J_t(x) := J^{T_x}(Dφ_t(x)). Claim: imageMass a φ_t K = ∫⁻_{M∩K} ofReal(θ(x)·J_t(x)) dHⁿ(x).
(2.1) By definition imageMass a φ_t K = ∫⁻_{φ_t(M∩K)} u_t dHⁿ with u_t(y) := ofReal(θ(ψ_t(y))), and u_t(φ_t(x)) = ofReal(θ(x)).
(2.2) Decomposition. Let D_i := F_i(C_i) ∖ (N₀ ∪ ⋃_{j<i} F_j(C_j)) (Borel: the F_j(C_j) are compact) and M_i := M ∩ K ∩ D_i (Hⁿ-null-measurable). The M_i are pairwise disjoint and, by (h3), M ∩ K = (M ∩ K ∩ N₀) ∪ ⋃_i M_i. As φ_t is injective, φ_t(M ∩ K) = φ_t(M ∩ K ∩ N₀) ∪ ⋃_i φ_t(M_i) with pairwise disjoint pieces; by 1(b) they are Hⁿ-null-measurable and Hⁿ(φ_t(M ∩ K ∩ N₀)) = 0. By countable additivity of the lintegral over disjoint null-measurable sets (lintegral_iUnion₀) and since null sets do not contribute:
imageMass a φ_t K = Σ_i ∫⁻_{φ_t(M_i)} u_t dHⁿ and ∫⁻_{M∩K} ofReal(θJ_t) dHⁿ = Σ_i ∫⁻_{M_i} ofReal(θJ_t) dHⁿ.
It therefore suffices to prove ∫⁻_{φ_t(M_i)} u_t dHⁿ = ∫⁻_{M_i} ofReal(θJ_t) dHⁿ for each i.
(2.3) Fix i. Choose a Borel set A with M_i ⊆ A ⊆ D_i and Hⁿ(A ∖ M_i) = 0 (a Borel hull of the null-measurable M_i, intersected with the Borel D_i). Let B := C_i ∩ F_i⁻¹(A): B is Borel, F_i(B) = A (A ⊆ F_i(C_i)), and F_i is injective on B (by the lower bound on C_i). Let ψ_i: F_i(C_i) → C_i be the inverse of F_i on C_i and, for y ∈ F_i(C_i), T_i(y) := range DF_i(ψ_i(y)).
(2.4) G := φ_t ∘ F_i is Lipschitz (composition of Lipschitz maps) and injective on B. For v ∈ B, F_i is differentiable at v and φ_t is differentiable at F_i(v), so DG(v) = Dφ_t(F_i(v)) ∘ DF_i(v) (chain rule), and by LinearMap.normDet_comp (normDet(Λ ∘ A') = J^{range A'}(Λ)·normDet(A')),
JG(v) = J^{range DF_i(v)}(Dφ_t(F_i(v)))·JF_i(v) = J^{T_i(F_i(v))}(Dφ_t(F_i(v)))·JF_i(v).
(2.5) Define h: E → [0, ∞] by h(y) := ofReal(J^{T_i(y)}(Dφ_t(y)))·u_t(φ_t(y)) for y ∈ F_i(C_i) and h(y) := 0 otherwise. Applying (R2a) to G on B and then to F_i on B (no measurability of the integrands is needed):
∫⁻_{φ_t(A)} u_t dHⁿ = ∫⁻_{G(B)} u_t dHⁿ = ∫⁻_B ofReal(JG(v))·u_t(G(v)) dv = ∫⁻_B ofReal(JF_i(v))·h(F_i(v)) dv = ∫⁻_{F_i(B)} h dHⁿ = ∫⁻_A h dHⁿ,
using ofReal(αβ) = ofReal(α)ofReal(β) for α, β ≥ 0 and (2.4).
(2.6) Since Hⁿ(A ∖ M_i) = 0 and, by 1(b), Hⁿ(φ_t(A ∖ M_i)) = 0, we get ∫⁻_{φ_t(M_i)} u_t dHⁿ = ∫⁻_{φ_t(A)} u_t dHⁿ and ∫⁻_A h dHⁿ = ∫⁻_{M_i} h dHⁿ. For Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M_i we have x = F_i(ψ_i(x)) with ψ_i(x) ∈ C_i, so (h4) gives T_x = range DF_i(ψ_i(x)) = T_i(x), and then h(x) = ofReal(J_t(x))·ofReal(θ(x)) = ofReal(θ(x)J_t(x)) (θ(x) > 0, J_t(x) ≥ 0). Hence ∫⁻_{φ_t(M_i)} u_t dHⁿ = ∫⁻_{M_i} ofReal(θJ_t) dHⁿ, and summing over i (2.2) proves the claim.

3. The Jacobian (parent step 9; Simon Ch. 2, 5.2–5.3).
(3.1) On the compact set [−ε/2, ε/2] × K the maps (t, y) ↦ Dφ_t(y), ∂_tDφ_t(y) and Dφ_t(y)⁻¹ are continuous (1(b), 1(c); inversion is continuous on invertible operators), hence bounded in operator norm by some Λ_1 ≥ 1.

For t ∈ (−ε, ε) let Gram_t := [⟨Dφ_t(x)e_a, Dφ_t(x)e_b⟩]_{a,b=1}^n, so J^P(Dφ_t(x)) = (det Gram_t)^{1/2} (LinearMap.normDet_sq_eq_det_gram). subproblem.title: Blow-up of a Lipschitz piece at a Lebesgue density point, with a uniform upper n-density bound
subproblem.statement: Let n ≥ 1, ℓ ≥ 0, E = ℝ^{n+ℓ} (Ambient n ℓ), ℝⁿ = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) with Lebesgue measure Lⁿ, and Hⁿ = μHE[n]. Let C ⊆ ℝⁿ be compact and F: ℝⁿ → E Lipschitz such that F is differentiable at every w ∈ C with injective derivative DF(w), w ↦ DF(w) is continuous on C, and c|v − w| ≤ |F(v) − F(w)| for all v, w ∈ C, for some c > 0. Then (3b) there is Γ ∈ ℝ with Hⁿ(F(C) ∩ B_ρ(x)) ≤ Γρⁿ for all x ∈ F(C) and ρ > 0 (closed balls); and (3a) for every w ∈ C with Lⁿ(C ∩ B_r(w))/Lⁿ(B_r(w)) → 1 as r ↓ 0 and every f ∈ C_c(E, ℝ), t⁻ⁿ∫_{F(C)} f(t⁻¹(y − F(w))) dHⁿ(y) → ∫_{DF(w)(ℝⁿ)} f dHⁿ as t ↓ 0.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n ℓ : ℕ) (C : Set (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n))) (F : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) → Ambient n ℓ), 0 < n → (IsCompact C ∧ (∃ K : NNReal, LipschitzWith K F) ∧ (∀ w ∈ C, DifferentiableAt ℝ F w ∧ Function.Injective (fderiv ℝ F w)) ∧ ContinuousOn (fderiv ℝ F) C ∧ ∃ c : ℝ, 0 < c ∧ ∀ v ∈ C, ∀ w ∈ C, c * ‖v - w‖ ≤ ‖F v - F w‖) → (∃ Γ : ℝ, ∀ x ∈ F '' C, ∀ ρ : ℝ, 0 < ρ → (μHE[n] : Measure (Ambient n ℓ)) (F '' C ∩ closedBall x ρ) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal (Γ * ρ ^ n)) ∧ ∀ w ∈ C, Tendsto (fun r : ℝ ↦ volume (C ∩ closedBall w r) / volume (closedBall w r)) (𝓝[>] 0) (𝓝 1) → ∀ f : C_c(Ambient n ℓ, ℝ), Tendsto (fun t : ℝ ↦ (t ^ n)⁻¹ * ∫ y in F '' C, f (t⁻¹ • (y - F w)) ∂μHE[n]) (𝓝[>] 0) (𝓝 (∫ y in (LinearMap.range (fderiv ℝ F w).toLinearMap : Set (Ambient n ℓ)), f y ∂μHE[n]))
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: the parent proof, step 3 (blow-up of one Lipschitz piece at a Lebesgue density point; Simon Ch. 3, proof of Theorem 1.6 '⇒' for a parametrized piece, which replaces the embedded C¹ pieces of Lemma 1.2), together with the piece facts of step 1. No errata apply.

Conventions. n ≥ 1, ℓ ≥ 0; E := Ambient n ℓ = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin (n+ℓ)); ℝⁿ := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) with Lebesgue measure Lⁿ := volume; Hⁿ := μHE[n] (on ℝⁿ, Hⁿ = Lⁿ by Mathlib EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume, and finrank ℝ ℝⁿ = n by finrank_euclideanSpace_fin); B_ρ(z) := closedBall z ρ; ω_n := Lⁿ(ball 0 1).toReal ∈ (0, ∞) and Lⁿ(B_s(z)) = sⁿ·Lⁿ(ball 0 1) for s ≥ 0 (Mathlib Measure.addHaar_closedBall, addHaar_closedBall_eq_addHaar_ball); ‖f‖ := sup|f|; for G: ℝⁿ → E, JG(v) := SimonGMT Chapter02.areaJacobianAt G v = (fderiv ℝ G v).normDet ≥ 0. Hypotheses: (P1) C ⊆ ℝⁿ compact; (P2) F: ℝⁿ → E is κ-Lipschitz (κ ≥ 0); (P3) for every w ∈ C, F is differentiable at w and DF(w) := fderiv ℝ F w is injective; (P4) w ↦ DF(w) is continuous on C; (P5) c > 0 and c|v − w| ≤ |F(v) − F(w)| for all v, w ∈ C. Put N := F(C).
Library results used (pinned; #print axioms shows only propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound):
(R2a) SimonGMT Chapter02.weighted_area_formula_lipschitz_injOn: G: ℝⁿ → E Lipschitz, B ⊆ ℝⁿ Borel, G injective on B ⇒ ∫⁻_{G(B)} u dHⁿ = ∫⁻_B ofReal(JG(v))·u(G(v)) dLⁿ(v) for every u: E → [0, ∞].
(R2b) SimonGMT Chapter02.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image_le_of_lipschitzOn: G K-Lipschitz on S ⇒ Hⁿ(G(S)) ≤ Kⁿ·Hⁿ(S).
(R2c) Mathlib LinearMap.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image_eq_normDet_mul_volume: for linear A: ℝⁿ → E and S ⊆ ℝⁿ, Hⁿ(A(S)) = ofReal(normDet A)·Lⁿ(S).
(R2d) SimonGMT Chapter02.continuous_normDet: A ↦ normDet A is continuous on L(ℝⁿ, E); Chapter02.measurable_areaJacobianAt: JG is Borel.

Proof.

1. Preliminary facts.
(a) F is injective on C: if F(v) = F(w) with v, w ∈ C then c|v − w| ≤ 0 by (P5), so v = w.
(b) N is compact (continuous image of the compact C), hence Borel, and Hⁿ(N) ≤ κⁿ·Lⁿ(C) < ∞ by (R2b).
(c) v ↦ JF(v) = normDet(DF(v)) is continuous on C by (P4) and (R2d); if C ≠ ∅ it is bounded on the compact set C by some Γ_J ≥ 0 (if C = ∅, claim (3a) is vacuous and (3b) is vacuous).

2. Claim (3b): with Γ := κⁿ·ω_n·c⁻ⁿ ≥ 0, Hⁿ(N ∩ B_ρ(x)) ≤ ofReal(Γρⁿ) for every x ∈ N and ρ > 0.
Let x = F(w) with w ∈ C, and ρ > 0. If y ∈ N ∩ B_ρ(x), write y = F(v) with v ∈ C; then c|v − w| ≤ |F(v) − F(w)| = |y − x| ≤ ρ, so v ∈ C ∩ B_{ρ/c}(w). Hence N ∩ B_ρ(x) ⊆ F(C ∩ B_{ρ/c}(w)). By (R2b) (F is κ-Lipschitz) and Hⁿ = Lⁿ on ℝⁿ,
Hⁿ(N ∩ B_ρ(x)) ≤ κⁿ·Lⁿ(B_{ρ/c}(w)) = κⁿ·(ρ/c)ⁿ·Lⁿ(ball 0 1) = ofReal(Γρⁿ).

3. Set-up for claim (3a). Fix w ∈ C with Lⁿ(C ∩ B_r(w))/Lⁿ(B_r(w)) → 1 as r ↓ 0, and f ∈ C_c(E). Put x := F(w), A := DF(w) (injective by (P3)) and T := range A = A(ℝⁿ). Choose R > 0 with f(z) = 0 whenever |z| > R (f has compact support). Since n ≥ 1, the unit sphere of ℝⁿ is nonempty and compact and e ↦ |Ae| is continuous and positive on it (A injective), so m_A := min_{|e|=1}|Ae| > 0 and |Au| ≥ m_A|u| for all u ∈ ℝⁿ. Put R' := R/min(c, m_A). f is uniformly continuous (continuous with compact support), so there is ω_f: [0, ∞) → [0, ∞) with |f(z) − f(z')| ≤ ω_f(|z − z'|) and ω_f(s) → 0 as s ↓ 0.

4. Area formula on the piece. For t > 0 let g_t(y) := f(t⁻¹(y − x)); g_t is continuous and |g_t| ≤ ‖f‖, so g_t is integrable for Hⁿ⌞N (Hⁿ(N) < ∞). Apply (R2a) with G := F and B := C (Borel, F injective on C by 1(a)) to u := ofReal(g_t⁺) and to u := ofReal(g_t⁻):
∫⁻_N ofReal(g_t^±) dHⁿ = ∫⁻_C ofReal(JF(v)·g_t^±(F(v))) dv,
and both sides are ≤ ‖f‖·Γ_J·Lⁿ(C) < ∞. Subtracting (the Bochner integral of an integrable real function is the difference of the lintegrals of its positive and negative parts):
∫_N g_t dHⁿ = ∫_C JF(v)·f(t⁻¹(F(v) − F(w))) dv.   (4.1)
(Equivalently: Hⁿ⌞N is the image under F of the finite measure JF·Lⁿ⌞C, by (R2a) applied to indicators; then use MeasureTheory.integral_map.)

5. Rescaling. Substituting v = w + tu (Lⁿ is translation invariant and Lⁿ(tS) = tⁿLⁿ(S) for t > 0; Mathlib MeasureTheory.integral_add_left_eq_self and Measure.integral_comp_smul), (4.1) gives
(tⁿ)⁻¹∫_N g_t dHⁿ = ∫_{ℝⁿ} 1_C(w + tu)·JF(w + tu)·f(Q_t(u)) du,  Q_t(u) := t⁻¹(F(w + tu) − F(w)).
If w + tu ∈ C and |u| > R', then by (P5) |Q_t(u)| ≥ t⁻¹·c·|tu| = c|u| > cR' ≥ R, so f(Q_t(u)) = 0. Hence
(tⁿ)⁻¹∫_N g_t dHⁿ = ∫_{B_{R'}(0)} 1_C(w + tu)·JF(w + tu)·f(Q_t(u)) du.   (5.1)

6. The tangent plane. A is linear, injective and Lipschitz (constant ‖A‖), fderiv ℝ A u = A for all u, so JA(u) = normDet(A) = JF(w) for every u. Apply (R2a) with G := A and B := ℝⁿ (A injective) to the positive and negative parts of f (f∘A is bounded and vanishes outside the bounded set B_{R/m_A}(0), so all integrals are finite), obtaining ∫_T f dHⁿ = JF(w)·∫_{ℝⁿ} f(Au) du (alternatively from (R2c): Hⁿ⌞T is the image under A of normDet(A)·Lⁿ). For |u| > R' ≥ R/m_A we have |Au| ≥ m_A|u| > R and f(Au) = 0, so
∫_T f dHⁿ = ∫_{B_{R'}(0)} JF(w)·f(Au) du.   (6.1)

7. Comparison. By (5.1) and (6.1), D_t := (tⁿ)⁻¹∫_N g_t dHⁿ − ∫_T f dHⁿ = D_t' − D_t'' with
D_t' := ∫_{B_{R'}(0)} 1_C(w + tu)·[JF(w + tu)·f(Q_t(u)) − JF(w)·f(Au)] du,
D_t'' := ∫_{B_{R'}(0)} 1_{ℝⁿ∖C}(w + tu)·JF(w)·f(Au) du.
(a) The affine map u ↦ w + tu maps B_{R'}(0) onto B_{tR'}(w) and multiplies Lⁿ by tⁿ, so
|D_t''| ≤ JF(w)·‖f‖·Lⁿ({u ∈ B_{R'}(0) : w + tu ∉ C}) = JF(w)·‖f‖·t⁻ⁿ·Lⁿ(B_{tR'}(w) ∖ C).
C is Borel and 0 < Lⁿ(B_r(w)) < ∞ for r > 0, so Lⁿ(B_r(w) ∖ C)/Lⁿ(B_r(w)) = 1 − Lⁿ(C ∩ B_r(w))/Lⁿ(B_r(w)) → 0 as r ↓ 0 by the density hypothesis, and t⁻ⁿLⁿ(B_{tR'}(w) ∖ C) = R'ⁿ·ω_n·[Lⁿ(B_{tR'}(w) ∖ C)/Lⁿ(B_{tR'}(w))] → 0 as t ↓ 0. Thus D_t'' → 0.
(b) Let σ(s) := sup{|F(w + h) − F(w) − Ah|/|h| : 0 < |h| ≤ s}; σ(s) → 0 as s ↓ 0 because F is differentiable at w with derivative A (P3). Let τ(s) := sup{|JF(v) − JF(w)| : v ∈ C, |v − w| ≤ s}; τ(s) → 0 as s ↓ 0 by the continuity of JF on C at w (1(c)). For |u| ≤ R' with v := w + tu ∈ C we have |Q_t(u) − Au| = t⁻¹|F(w + tu) − F(w) − A(tu)| ≤ |u|·σ(t|u|) ≤ R'·σ(tR') (the left side is 0 if u = 0) and |JF(v) − JF(w)| ≤ τ(tR'); hence
|JF(v)·f(Q_t(u)) − JF(w)·f(Au)| ≤ JF(v)·|f(Q_t(u)) − f(Au)| + |f(Au)|·|JF(v) − JF(w)| ≤ Γ_J·ω_f(R'σ(tR')) + ‖f‖·τ(tR'),
uniformly in such u. Therefore |D_t'| ≤ Lⁿ(B_{R'}(0))·[Γ_J·ω_f(R'σ(tR')) + ‖f‖·τ(tR')] → 0 as t ↓ 0.
Consequently D_t → 0, i.e. (tⁿ)⁻¹∫_{F(C)} f(t⁻¹(y − F(w))) dHⁿ(y) → ∫_{range DF(w)} f dHⁿ as t ↓ 0. This is claim (3a); together with step 2 the theorem is proved. ∎

Implementation note (not part of the argument): the statement elaborates with the frozen imports; the proof additionally needs, e.g., Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter02.AreaLipschitz and Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter02.AreaApproximation (already built in the pinned package) and Mathlib.Analysis.InnerProductSpace.NormDet; all seven child types were checked to elaborate unchanged with these imports added.

(3b): N ∩ B_ρ(F(w)) ⊆ F(C ∩ B_{ρ/c}(w)), so Hⁿ(N ∩ B_ρ) ≤ κⁿω_n c⁻ⁿρⁿ by the Lipschitz image bound
Area formula on (F, C) for the positive and negative parts: ∫_N f(t⁻¹(y − F(w))) dHⁿ = ∫_C JF(v) f(t⁻¹(F(v) − F(w))) dv
Rescale v = w + tu; the integrand vanishes for |u| > R' by the lower Lipschitz bound
Area formula for the injective linear A = DF(w): ∫_T f dHⁿ = ∫_{B_{R'}(0)} JF(w) f(Au) du
The difference is D_t' − D_t''; D_t'' → 0 because w is a density point, D_t' → 0 by differentiability at w, continuity of JF on C and uniform continuity of f

subproblem.title: Strongly measurable projection field agreeing with the piece tangent planes on the disjointified pieces
subproblem.statement: For all n, ℓ and every sequence (C_i, F_i)_{i∈ℕ} of Lipschitz pieces into E = ℝ^{n+ℓ} (C_i ⊆ ℝⁿ compact, F_i Lipschitz, differentiable at each w ∈ C_i with injective DF_i(w), DF_i continuous on C_i, c_i|v − w| ≤ |F_i(v) − F_i(w)| on C_i with c_i > 0), there is a strongly measurable g: E → L(E, E) such that g(F_i(w)) is the orthogonal projection onto DF_i(w)(ℝⁿ) whenever i ∈ ℕ, w ∈ C_i and F_i(w) ∉ F_j(C_j) for all j < i.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n ℓ : ℕ) (C : ℕ → Set (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n))) (F : ℕ → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) → Ambient n ℓ), (∀ i, IsCompact (C i) ∧ (∃ K : NNReal, LipschitzWith K (F i)) ∧ (∀ w ∈ C i, DifferentiableAt ℝ (F i) w ∧ Function.Injective (fderiv ℝ (F i) w)) ∧ ContinuousOn (fderiv ℝ (F i)) (C i) ∧ ∃ c : ℝ, 0 < c ∧ ∀ v ∈ C i, ∀ w ∈ C i, c * ‖v - w‖ ≤ ‖F i v - F i w‖) → ∃ g : Ambient n ℓ → (Ambient n ℓ →L[ℝ] Ambient n ℓ), StronglyMeasurable g ∧ ∀ i, ∀ w ∈ C i, (∀ j < i, F i w ∉ F j '' C j) → g (F i w) = (LinearMap.range (fderiv ℝ (F i) w).toLinearMap).starProjection
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: the parent proof, step 1 (continuity of x ↦ p_{T_i(x)} on each compact piece N_i = F_i(C_i)) and step 6(iii) (the piecewise field g on the disjointified pieces N_i ∖ ⋃_{j<i} N_j is Borel). No errata apply.

Conventions. E := Ambient n ℓ; ℝⁿ := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n); L(X, Y) := X →L[ℝ] Y with the operator-norm topology; for injective A ∈ L(ℝⁿ, E), range A := LinearMap.range A.toLinearMap and Π(A) := (range A).starProjection ∈ L(E, E) is the orthogonal projection onto range A. For each i ∈ ℕ, (C_i, F_i) satisfies (P1) C_i compact; (P2) F_i Lipschitz; (P3) F_i differentiable at each w ∈ C_i with DF_i(w) := fderiv ℝ F_i w injective; (P4) DF_i continuous on C_i; (P5) c_i > 0 with c_i|v − w| ≤ |F_i(v) − F_i(w)| for v, w ∈ C_i. N_i := F_i(C_i).
Results used (Mathlib, pinned; standard axioms only): ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint (A ↦ A* is a linear isometric equivalence, hence continuous), Ring.inverse and NormedRing.inverse_continuousAt (inversion is continuous at units of the complete normed ring L(ℝⁿ, ℝⁿ)), the characterization of the orthogonal projection (y = p_K z iff y ∈ K and z − y ⊥ K; e.g. Submodule.eq_starProjection_of_mem_of_inner_eq_zero), continuousOn_iff', Measurable.stronglyMeasurable (L(E, E) is a finite-dimensional normed space, hence second countable and metrizable).

Proof.
1. A formula for Π. Let A ∈ L(ℝⁿ, E) be injective. Then A*A ∈ L(ℝⁿ, ℝⁿ) is invertible: ⟨A*Av, v⟩ = |Av|² > 0 for v ≠ 0, so A*A is injective, hence bijective (finite dimension). We claim Π(A) = A(A*A)⁻¹A*. For z ∈ E put y := A(A*A)⁻¹A*z. Then y ∈ range A, and for every v ∈ ℝⁿ, ⟨z − y, Av⟩ = ⟨A*z − A*A(A*A)⁻¹A*z, v⟩ = 0, i.e. z − y ⊥ range A; hence y = p_{range A}(z).
2. Continuity of Π at injective maps. Let Φ(A) := A ∘ Ring.inverse(A*A) ∘ A* for A ∈ L(ℝⁿ, E). If A_0 is injective then A_0*A_0 is a unit of L(ℝⁿ, ℝⁿ), Ring.inverse is continuous at A_0*A_0 (NormedRing.inverse_continuousAt), and A ↦ A*A, A ↦ A* and composition are continuous; hence Φ is continuous at A_0. By step 1, Π(A) = Φ(A) for every injective A.
3. Continuity on each piece. Fix i. F_i is injective on C_i by (P5); let ψ_i: N_i → C_i be the inverse, ψ_i(F_i(w)) = w. For y = F_i(v), y' = F_i(w) in N_i, |ψ_i(y) − ψ_i(y')| = |v − w| ≤ c_i⁻¹|y − y'|, so ψ_i is continuous on N_i (Lipschitz). Define G_i(y) := Φ(DF_i(ψ_i(y))) for y ∈ N_i. Since ψ_i maps N_i continuously into C_i, DF_i is continuous on C_i (P4), and Φ is continuous at each DF_i(w), w ∈ C_i (injective by (P3), step 2), G_i is continuous on N_i (composition of ContinuousOn/ContinuousAt maps). By step 1, G_i(F_i(w)) = Π(DF_i(w)) for every w ∈ C_i.
4. The field. N_i is compact (continuous image of the compact C_i), hence closed and Borel. Put D_i := N_i ∖ ⋃_{j<i} N_j (Borel, pairwise disjoint, ⋃_i D_i = ⋃_i N_i). Define g: E → L(E, E) by g(y) := G_i(y) if y ∈ D_i (the index i is unique), and g(y) := 0 if y ∉ ⋃_i N_i. (In Lean one may write g(y) := if h : ∃ i, y ∈ N_i then G_{Nat.find h}(y) else 0; then y ∈ D_{Nat.find h}.)
5. Measurability. Let O ⊆ L(E, E) be open. For each i, G_i is continuous on N_i ⊇ D_i, so by continuousOn_iff' there is an open U_i ⊆ E with G_i⁻¹(O) ∩ N_i = U_i ∩ N_i; hence D_i ∩ g⁻¹(O) = D_i ∩ U_i is Borel. Therefore g⁻¹(O) = ⋃_i (D_i ∩ U_i) ∪ (E ∖ ⋃_i N_i if 0 ∈ O, ∅ otherwise) is Borel. So g is Borel measurable, and since L(E, E) is a finite-dimensional normed space (second countable, metrizable), g is strongly measurable (Measurable.stronglyMeasurable).
6. Values. Let i ∈ ℕ and w ∈ C_i with F_i(w) ∉ F_j(C_j) = N_j for all j < i. Then y := F_i(w) ∈ D_i, so g(y) = G_i(y) = Π(DF_i(w)) = (range DF_i(w)).starProjection by step 3. Hence g has the required property. ∎

Implementation note (not part of the argument): the statement elaborates with the frozen imports; the proof may need additional imports such as Mathlib.Analysis.InnerProductSpace.Adjoint (built in the pinned packages); the frozen child types elaborate unchanged with such imports.
proof_key_steps: Π(A) = A(A*A)⁻¹A* is the projection onto range A for injective A, and it is continuous at injective A
The inverse ψ_i of F_i on C_i is Lipschitz, so y ↦ Π(DF_i(ψ_i(y))) is continuous on the compact N_i = F_i(C_i)
Define g by this formula on N_i ∖ ⋃_{j<i} N_j and 0 elsewhere; g is Borel, hence strongly measurable
g(F_i(w)) = p_{range DF_i(w)} when F_i(w) lies in no earlier piece

subproblem.title: Weighted blow-up of μ_V at Hⁿ-a.e. point of M lying on one Lipschitz piece
subproblem.statement: Let n ≥ 1, ℓ ≥ 0, let a = (M, θ) be an admissible pair in E = ℝ^{n+ℓ} (M countably n-rectifiable and Hⁿ-null-measurable, θ > 0 on M, θ ∈ L¹(Hⁿ⌞(M ∩ K)) for every compact K) with weight μ = μ_{v(M,θ)} = Hⁿ⌞θ, and let (C, F) be a Lipschitz piece: C ⊆ ℝⁿ compact, F: ℝⁿ → E Lipschitz, differentiable at every w ∈ C with injective DF(w), DF continuous on C, and c|v − w| ≤ |F(v) − F(w)| on C with c > 0. Then for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M: for every w ∈ C with F(w) = x and every f ∈ C_c(E, ℝ), t⁻ⁿ∫ f(t⁻¹(y − x)) dμ(y) → θ(x)∫_{DF(w)(ℝⁿ)} f dHⁿ as t ↓ 0.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n ℓ : ℕ) (a : RectifiablePair n ℓ) (C : Set (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n))) (F : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) → Ambient n ℓ), 0 < n → (IsCompact C ∧ (∃ K : NNReal, LipschitzWith K F) ∧ (∀ w ∈ C, DifferentiableAt ℝ F w ∧ Function.Injective (fderiv ℝ F w)) ∧ ContinuousOn (fderiv ℝ F) C ∧ ∃ c : ℝ, 0 < c ∧ ∀ v ∈ C, ∀ w ∈ C, c * ‖v - w‖ ≤ ‖F v - F w‖) → ∀ᵐ x ∂(μHE[n] : Measure (Ambient n ℓ)).restrict a.M, ∀ w ∈ C, F w = x → ∀ f : C_c(Ambient n ℓ, ℝ), Tendsto (fun t : ℝ ↦ (t ^ n)⁻¹ * ∫ y, f (t⁻¹ • (y - x)) ∂(mk a).weight) (𝓝[>] 0) (𝓝 (a.θ x * ∫ y in (LinearMap.range (fderiv ℝ F w).toLinearMap : Set (Ambient n ℓ)), f y ∂μHE[n]))
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: the parent proof, step 4 (Simon Ch. 3, Theorem 1.9 '⇒' via the proof of Theorem 1.6 '⇒' and Remark 1.8(1)); the argument there uses the compact multiplicity pieces only through C ⊆ M ∩ N_i, so it applies verbatim to one Lipschitz piece N = F(C) without disjointifying. No errata apply.

Conventions. n ≥ 1, ℓ ≥ 0; E := Ambient n ℓ; ℝⁿ := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) with Lebesgue measure Lⁿ := volume; Hⁿ := μHE[n] (= Lⁿ on ℝⁿ); B_ρ(z) := closedBall z ρ; ‖f‖ := sup|f|. a = (M, θ) is an admissible pair (IsRectifiablePair): M is countably n-rectifiable and Hⁿ-null-measurable, θ(x) > 0 for x ∈ M, and θ is Hⁿ-integrable on M ∩ K for every compact K. μ := (mk a).weight. (C, F) satisfies (P1) C ⊆ ℝⁿ compact; (P2) F is κ-Lipschitz (κ ≥ 0); (P3) F is differentiable at each w ∈ C with injective DF(w) := fderiv ℝ F w; (P4) DF is continuous on C; (P5) c|v − w| ≤ |F(v) − F(w)| on C with c > 0. N := F(C). "The claim at x" means: for every w ∈ C with F(w) = x and every f ∈ C_c(E, ℝ), (tⁿ)⁻¹∫ f(t⁻¹(y − x)) dμ(y) → θ(x)·∫_{range DF(w)} f dHⁿ as t ↓ 0 (t > 0). We must show that the claim holds for Hⁿ⌞M-a.e. x.
Results used (pinned; standard axioms only):
- Sibling ts_piece_density_blowup (applied to n, ℓ, C, F, using 0 < n and the piece hypotheses): (3b) there is Γ ∈ ℝ with Hⁿ(N ∩ B_ρ(z)) ≤ ofReal(Γρⁿ) for all z ∈ N and ρ > 0; (3a) for every w ∈ C with Lⁿ(C ∩ B_r(w))/Lⁿ(B_r(w)) → 1 (r ↓ 0) and every f ∈ C_c(E, ℝ): (tⁿ)⁻¹∫_N f(t⁻¹(y − F(w))) dHⁿ(y) → ∫_{range DF(w)} f dHⁿ.
- (R2b) SimonGMT Chapter02.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image_le_of_lipschitzOn: Hⁿ(F(S)) ≤ κⁿ·Lⁿ(S) for S ⊆ ℝⁿ.
- Lebesgue density theorem, Mathlib Besicovitch.ae_tendsto_measure_inter_div (μ := volume on ℝⁿ, s := C).
- Lusin's theorem, SimonGMT Chapter01.exists_isClosed_continuousOn_of_measurable, for a measure that is closed-inner-regular on finite-measure measurable sets; a finite Borel measure on E is weakly regular, so this holds by Mathlib MeasurableSet.exists_isClosed_sdiff_lt.
- Upper density theorem (Simon Ch. 1, 3.6), SimonGMT Chapter01.ae_dimensionalUpperDensity_eq_zero_outside together with Chapter01.measure_toOuterMeasure_isBorelRegular and Chapter02.simonHausdorffMeasureReal_nat_eq_euclideanHausdorffMeasure: if ν is a Borel measure on E and A ⊆ E is Borel with ν(A) < ∞, then for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∉ A, ν(A ∩ B_r(x))/rⁿ → 0 as r ↓ 0. (In the library the conclusion is "dimensionalUpperDensity ν.toOuterMeasure n A x = 0", the limsup as r ↓ 0 of ν(A ∩ B_r(x))/(realUnitBallVolume n·ofReal(r)ⁿ) with the constant realUnitBallVolume n ∈ (0, ∞); a vanishing limsup of nonnegative quantities is a limit 0; Borel sets are Carathéodory measurable for ν.toOuterMeasure; the a.e. is for simonHausdorffMeasureReal n = μHE[n].)

Proof.

1. The weight. By definition (mk a).weight = pairWeight n M θ = (Hⁿ⌞M).withDensity(z ↦ ofReal θ(z)) (Quot.lift evaluated on the class of a; definitional).
(a) θ is a.e.-strongly measurable for Hⁿ⌞M: M = ⋃_{k∈ℕ} (M ∩ B_k(0)) and θ is integrable, hence a.e.-strongly measurable, on each M ∩ B_k(0) (B_k(0) is compact); use Mathlib aestronglyMeasurable_iUnion_iff.
(b) For Borel S ⊆ E: μ(S) = ∫⁻_{M∩S} ofReal θ dHⁿ (withDensity_apply, Measure.restrict_restrict); in particular μ(K) ≤ ∫_{M∩K}|θ| dHⁿ < ∞ for compact K.
(c) For Borel S and a bounded Borel g: E → ℝ vanishing outside a bounded set, g is μ-integrable and ∫_S g dμ = ∫_{M∩S} g·θ dHⁿ: by Mathlib integral_withDensity_eq_integral_toReal_smul₀ (density ofReal∘θ is a.e.-measurable by (a) and finite), ∫ g dμ = ∫ (ofReal θ(z)).toReal·g(z) d(Hⁿ⌞M)(z) and (ofReal θ(z)).toReal = θ(z) for z ∈ M, which holds Hⁿ⌞M-a.e. (ae_restrict_mem₀, M null-measurable); integrability follows from (b) and boundedness.

2. Piece facts. F is injective on C by (P5); for z ∈ N let ψ(z) be the unique w ∈ C with F(w) = z. N is compact, hence Borel, and Hⁿ(N) ≤ κⁿ·Lⁿ(C) < ∞ by (R2b). Fix Γ as in (3b) and put Γ⁺ := max(Γ, 0) ≥ 0; then Hⁿ(N ∩ B_ρ(z)) ≤ ofReal(Γρⁿ) ≤ ofReal(Γ⁺ρⁿ), so (tⁿ)⁻¹·Hⁿ(N ∩ B_{Rt}(z)).toReal ≤ Γ⁺Rⁿ for all z ∈ N and R, t > 0 (the measure is finite).

3. Density points. By the Lebesgue density theorem, Lⁿ(C ∩ B_r(w))/Lⁿ(B_r(w)) → 1 (r ↓ 0) for Lⁿ⌞C-a.e. w. Let Z be the set of w ∈ C at which this fails. Since C is Borel, Lⁿ(Z) = Lⁿ(Z ∩ C) = (Lⁿ⌞C)(Z) = 0 (Measure.restrict_apply'). By (R2b), Hⁿ(F(Z)) ≤ κⁿ·Lⁿ(Z) = 0. If x ∈ N ∖ F(Z), then ψ(x) ∉ Z, i.e. ψ(x) is a density point of C.

4. Reduction. Since M is Hⁿ-null-measurable, Hⁿ⌞M-a.e. x lies in M (Mathlib ae_restrict_mem₀), so points outside M may be ignored. If x ∉ N, no w ∈ C satisfies F(w) = x, so the claim at x holds vacuously. Every Hⁿ-null set is Hⁿ⌞M-null. Hence it suffices to construct countably many compact sets C_k ⊆ M ∩ N such that (i) Hⁿ((M ∩ N) ∖ ⋃_k C_k) = 0, (ii) θ restricted to each C_k is continuous, and (iii) for each k the claim holds at Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ C_k. Then the claim fails only on (E ∖ M) ∪ ((M ∩ N) ∖ ⋃_k C_k) ∪ ⋃_k (exceptional set in C_k): the first set is Hⁿ⌞M-null and the others are Hⁿ-null.

5. Construction of the C_k (Lusin pieces). By 1(a) choose a Borel function θ̃: E → ℝ with θ = θ̃ Hⁿ⌞M-a.e. (AEMeasurable.mk). Choose a Borel set S ⊇ {z : θ(z) ≠ θ̃(z)} with (Hⁿ⌞M)(S) = 0 (measurable null hull), and a Borel set M' ⊆ M with Hⁿ(M ∖ M') = 0 (M is Hⁿ-null-measurable). Then Hⁿ(M' ∩ S) = (Hⁿ⌞M)(M' ∩ S) ≤ (Hⁿ⌞M)(S) = 0 (M' ∩ S ⊆ M is Borel). For integers q ≥ 1 put
A_q := (M' ∖ S) ∩ N ∩ {θ̃ ≥ 1/q} ∩ B_q(0),
a Borel set. On A_q ⊆ M ∖ S we have θ = θ̃ ≥ 1/q, so Hⁿ(A_q) ≤ q·∫_{M∩B_q(0)} θ dHⁿ < ∞ (Chebyshev). For integers m ≥ 1 apply Lusin's theorem to the finite Borel measure ν_q := Hⁿ⌞A_q, the Borel set A_q (ν_q(A_q) < ∞) and the Borel function θ̃: there is a closed set C_{q,m} ⊆ A_q with Hⁿ(A_q ∖ C_{q,m}) = ν_q(A_q ∖ C_{q,m}) < 1/m on which θ̃ is continuous. C_{q,m} is closed and bounded (⊆ B_q(0)), hence compact; C_{q,m} ⊆ A_q ⊆ M ∩ N; and θ = θ̃ on C_{q,m} (⊆ M' ∖ S), so θ restricted to C_{q,m} is continuous. Covering: if x ∈ (M ∩ N) ∖ ((M ∖ M') ∪ (M' ∩ S)), then x ∈ (M' ∖ S) ∩ N and θ̃(x) = θ(x) > 0, so x ∈ A_q for every integer q ≥ max(1/θ(x), |x|). Therefore
(M ∩ N) ∖ ⋃_{q,m} C_{q,m} ⊆ (M ∖ M') ∪ (M' ∩ S) ∪ ⋃_q (A_q ∖ ⋃_m C_{q,m}),
and Hⁿ(A_q ∖ ⋃_m C_{q,m}) ≤ inf_m 1/m = 0. So the countable family (C_{q,m}) satisfies (i) and (ii).

6. Two upper-density estimates. Fix one of these compact sets C' := C_{q,m} and r_0 > 0 with C' ⊆ ball(0, r_0). Apply the upper density theorem twice:
(a) ν := μ (a Borel measure) and A_a := B_{r_0}(0) ∖ C' (Borel; μ(A_a) ≤ μ(B_{r_0}(0)) < ∞ by 1(b));
(b) ν := Hⁿ⌞N and A_b := N ∖ C' (Borel; ν(A_b) ≤ Hⁿ(N) < ∞).
